question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
answer:
North American Aviation built the spacecraft. Collins stayed in the Apollo 11 command module Columbia during the landing. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Columbia was Apollo 11's command module. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The command and service module was built by North American Aviation. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

North American Aviation was also the prime contractor for that module. [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
answer:
Oxygen tank No. 2 had its heaters run on ground power for about eight hours before launch. The review board said an electrically started fire in that tank started the explosion.

- **Heater run:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **What started the explosion:** [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"
- **Switch rating:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **Specification change:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **The board's verdict:** [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

answer:

[[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". Jack Swigert became command module pilot in place of Mattingly. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The same day, Mission Control changed the goal from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down after using Aquarius as a lifeboat. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **June 1970:** The Review Board report was published. The brain gives no day. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
